item.title: You're Invited: Eastland Plan Kickoff
item.description:
Eastland Community Plan Kickoff 

The Eastland Community Plan is getting started and we need your voice to make this plan a success.

Date: Saturday, October 14th, 2023 

Time: 11:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. 

Location: Barnett Community Center, 1184 Barnett Road, Columbus, OH 43227 

Join us to kick off the Eastland Community Plan on October 14th. Now is the time to envision a new future for the Eastland area, one that is equitable and prosperous for everyone. We need your voice and your ideas to make that happen. Be part of the planning process to create the roadmap for the future of your community.  

This meeting will include:

  • A brief presentation about the Eastland Community Plan process;

item.title: 2024 NALA Application is Now Open
item.description:
2024 NALA Application is Now Open!

 

Apply for the New American Leadership Academy 

We are pleased to share with you that the application for the 2024 New American Leadership Academy (NALA) cohort is now available.

NALA is an opportunity for New American professionals to foster their personal development by building knowledge in civic engagement, and discovering new ways to contribute to their respective communities and the city of Columbus at large.  Academy participants receive mentorship and professional development on topics including government, civic engagement, and strategic collaboration along with  implicit bias training, public speaking, and conflict resolution and management. The bi-monthly sessions will begin in March 2024 and end in November 2024.

Applications will be accepted now through November 17, 2023. For more information, and to apply online, please visit www.columbus.gov/nala.

item.title: The Commission on Black Girls hosts Free Screening of The Little Mermaid
item.description:
The Commission on Black Girls hosts Free Community Screening of The Little Mermaid

 

The Commission on Black Girls

Join us for a Showing of The Little Mermaid 

“Be the Hero of your Own Story”

Tickets are Complimentary

Hundreds of young Black girls across the nation saw themselves when The Little Mermaid Live-Action Trailer made a big splash earlier this year. Countless videos showed gleeful Black girls in awe and amazement as they watched an Ariel with long beautiful red locs and cinnamon skin mesmerize their screens. These reactions reaffirmed that Black girls need to see positive representations in media and film.

In alignment with the protections found within the CROWN Act and the need to support the positive representation of Black girls and women in media and film, The Commission on Black Girls would like to show girls that they can be the heroines of their own stories, as well as empower advocacy behind changing the portrayal of Black women and girls in film, television and other forms of media. 125 complimentary tickets are available on a first come, first serve basis.

 

Date: Saturday, May 27, 2023

Time: Doors Open at 10 am

Location: AMC Easton Town Center 275 Easton Town Center

item.title: You're Invited! MLK Day March & Program
item.description:
The 2023 City of Columbus
MLK Day March & Program

 

Please join us to celebrate and honor the legacy of the Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. at the annual City of Columbus MLK Day March and Program.
Be inspired by Mayor Andrew J. Ginther and central Ohio’s Luke Fedlam and recording artist Nia Allen plus more dynamic speakers. This event is free and open to the public.

Lincoln Theatre
769 E. Long St, Columbus, OH 43202
Monday, January 16, 2023
March begins at 4:30 p.m.
Program begins at 5:30 p.m.
Visit https://www.columbus.gov/MLK2023 for more information.

Luke Fedlam


Luke Fedlam is a partner at the law firm of Porter Wright here in Columbus, where he leads the sports law practice group.  He is a nationally known thought-leader, speaker and author on the business of sports and protecting athletes. A Life Member of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Incorporated, Luke currently services as the Chapter President of Alpha Rho Lambda Chapter, Alpha’s Alumni Chapter here in Columbus.  Outside of work, Luke serves the community on the Board of Directors for the Columbus Clippers, the Board of Trustees for Capital University, the Board of Directors for the National Youth Advocate Program, and the Board of Commissioners for the Greater Columbus Sports Commission.

Nia Allen


Nia Allen is a #1 Billboard artist garnering top success with her inspirational hit song “Wait”.   As a sought-after worship leader Nia has led worship for CeCe Winans “Always Sisters Forever Brothers” youth conferences, Women of Faith’s national conferences, Living Proof Live with Beth Moore and the National Worship Leader’s Conference comprised of over 10,000 Worship Leaders from all around the world.

item.title: My Brother's Keeper Grant Opportunity
item.description:
My Brother's Keeper Grant Opportunity

The City of Columbus Department of Neighborhoods My Brother's Keeper is pleased to announce the availability of $300,000 in general revenue grant funding.  MBK Round 3 is intended to support 501(c)(3) charitable nonprofit organizations serving Columbus and Franklin County boys and men of color. 

Applications are due November 18, 2022 @ 11:59pm

Background

President Barack Obama launched My Brother’s Keeper, a call to action to address the persistent opportunity gaps facing boys and young men of color (BYMOC) and to ensure all young people can reach their full potential. Locally, many have responded to the President’s call to action.  The City of Columbus launched MBK Village and engaged hundreds of young men through the annual summit and conference. These events provided insight on a variety of educational and career opportunities as well as summer employment options.  In recent months, the Department of Neighborhoods has consulted with past, current and potential partners and developed a framework that will guide investment and support for an alignment of stakeholders around strategies that would help to close the gap between boys and young men of color and their peers.  Rooted in the idea that we must work together to expand opportunities for BYMOC, the City envisions a reenergized MBK Village that is focused on priorities aligned with MBK’s key milestones and targets barriers to success at the individual, organizational and systemic levels.

Applicant organizations that serve both young men and women will be considered, but they must demonstrate an explicit emphasis on improving outcomes for BYMOC. Additionally, preference will be given to organizations whose programs are made up of at least 50 percent minority male participants attending public schools.

Round 3 demonstration grants will help project teams test ideas and learn what works to improve high school graduation rates and help participants demonstrate proficient  professional skills to meet the requirements of the Ohio Means Jobs Readiness Seals.

Guidelines

MBK Grant will utilize SmartSheet online application process.  All applications must be submitted online.

Click Here to Apply

item.title: Updates to Columbus Non-Discrimination Ordinance
item.description:
As we prepare this month to celebrate 40 years of PRIDE in Columbus, we are excited to share with you some important news about new civil rights protections for people in our city.   

Since 1991, Columbus residents have been protected by one of the most comprehensive anti-discrimination ordinances in the State of Ohio.  This work has been led by the Department of Neighborhood’s Community Relations Commission. The Commission is a body of community leaders who advocate for respect and mutual understanding among cultural, religious and community groups.

As a part of Mayor Ginther’s equity agenda, the Department of Neighborhoods, in partnership with the Community Relations Commission, Columbus City Council and the City Attorney’s Office, completed an in-depth review and identified updates that were needed to ensure residents have the most up to date protections from discrimination possible. Columbus City Council took action and approved legislation that enhances our code by:

  • Adding the ability for the Community Relations Commission to issue a civil fine when discrimination has occurred. For a first offense, a fine not to exceed $1,000 can be imposed.
  • Providing protections for those who choose to wear natural hair styles.
  • Ensuring protection for LGBTQIA+ youth.
  • Protecting those who receive gender affirming care.
  • Protecting individuals who exercise their reproductive rights

To learn more, please watch this short video featuring Community Relations Commission Chair Chris Cozad.

 

 

 


You can also learn more by attending the Commission’s virtual Lunch and Learn on Thursday, June 3rd at noon. The session will be live on the Department of Neighborhood’s Facebook page @cbusneighbor. 

Discrimination in Columbus has been and continues to be illegal in Columbus. More information on the protections that exist and the complaint process are available at www.columbus.gov/discrimination.

As your front door to the City of Columbus, the Department of Neighborhoods, looks forward to serving all communities through the work of the Community Relations Commission and our other programming. Visit us at www.columbus.gov/neighborhoods for updates on our work.

Thank you,

Carla Williams-Scott                                           Chris Cozad

Director                                                              Chair

Department of Neighborhoods                          Community Relations Commission
